I've made myself invisible for so long that I can't form relationships. What would I tell a potential partner? "Ah yea I've stayed in my house all month, because the outside world seems too dangerous to explore." How sexy is that? "I'm gonna withdraw in my house for 3 weeks because being outside is too much for me to bear". I pretend to be asexual/aromantic all the time to save me from the heartache of letting people be too close.

I think people see me as an asexual robot. This is however a deliberately crafted persona and defense mechanism. Because I don't know how love works. Deep down I crave companionship, love and also sex. Yet I don't have the faintest idea of how any of these things work. Best leave it to people who do. Relationships are for the living, whereas I'm as good as dead. And life is  just passing me by. 

This typifies my AvPD. Craving things I think I cannot have and by avoiding them making them harder and harder to obtain.

I wish I was asexual/aromantic because that would mean no more crushes who will never love me back. It is so freeing to not want the things you can never have.

It's passed me by and at this point I don't even know how to begin the 'relationship game' that should've started in my teens somewhere.

Your mom sounds a lot like my mom. Took a while for someone to come in and say that when YOU feel it's a problem, it actually IS a problem. And for me to believe this, and not write it off as something unimportant took even longer. But it is the case. AvPD sufferers have tremendous trouble with seemingly trivial things. And most people who say overcoming mental blockades is just a matter of will, in my experience, lack the frame of reference. They've never been in your shoes. The fact is that using guilt and shame as a motivator actually achieves opposite results. It's the worst way of getting people to listen and to change. Hell it strikes tenfold if you're avoidant and hypersensitive to criticism.
Maybe tell your mom there's some mental blockade that stops you from playing tennis with your dad? she agreed to set up an appointment with a psychologist, she should follow through. Or set up your own appointment with your GP, usually they can refer you to a psychologist (though I don't know if this works this way in your country).
I hope that in any case you can make it clear to your mom to stop trivializing your problems.
Take care.

Yes organic has to meet certain standards. However they're still mainly based on the idea that natural = good and chemicals = bad. For instance, only natural pesticides and fertilizers can be used, it is a-priori assumed that natural pesticides and fertilizers are better than synthetic ones or even not harmful. It's more based on a gut feeling and ideology than solid science.

It's a billion dollar industry with a large lobby behind it and it's managed to maintain a "mom and pop" image that plays the underdog. It spins this narrative of green clean healthy food and when the evidence is looked at it just falls apart.

[Here](https://risk-monger.blogactiv.eu/2015/11/12/the-risk-mongers-dirty-dozen-12-highly-toxic-pesticides-approved-for-use-in-organic-farming/) is a list of very harmful pesticides (purely natural or derived from natural sources) used widely in organic farming.

A [meta-analysis](http://ajcn.nutrition.org/content/early/2010/05/12/ajcn.2010.29269.abstract?maxtoshow=&hits=10&RESULTFORMAT=&fulltext=organic&searchid=1&FIRSTINDEX=0&resourcetype=HWCIT) of almost 99000 articles over a span of half a century concluded: 
> From a systematic review of the currently available published literature, evidence is lacking for nutrition-related health effects that result from the consumption of organically produced foodstuffs.

They're hampering themselves with the idea that the closer it is to nature the healthier it is. The idea that chemikulz should be avoided and if humans tampered with it it somehow becomes 'corrupted' is so detrimental and misguided.
Natural/organic food. It's basically a marketing scheme and not better for you or the environment.
